copyPanel.rule: Mathematical Modeling in Careers & Daily Life
steps: 1. Frame real-world problems mathematically using rates, percentages, and geometry
2. Collect and analyze data to optimize decisions and resource allocation
3. Communicate quantitative findings clearly with equations and visual models

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Brushing Your Teeth
revealWordProblem.text:
For good hygiene you should brush your teeth twice a day. Leaving the water running while you brush wastes an average of four gallons, compared with turning the water on only to rinse.
Question: How much water would you save each year if every person in your house ran the water only to rinse? How does your saving compare with a household of 3, 4, 5, and 8 people?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Five toothbrushes in a row, each a different color.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Each brushing saves about 4 gallons, and you brush twice a day, so one person saves 8 gallons a day. In a year that is 8 × 365 = 2,920 gallons per person. Multiply by the number of people: 3 people save 8,760 gallons, 4 people save 11,680 gallons, 5 people save 14,600 gallons, and 8 people save 23,360 gallons. Every extra person in the house adds another 2,920 gallons saved.

questions.stem: A planter is 4 feet long and 2 feet wide. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of a rectangle is length × width: 4 × 2 = 8 square feet.
choiceFeedback: 2 comes from dividing 4 by 2 instead of multiplying.
6 comes from adding 4 + 2 instead of multiplying.
12 comes from adding all four sides (4 + 2 + 4 + 2) — that is the perimeter, not the area.
hints: Area tells how much flat space the planter covers.
For a rectangle, multiply length by width.
Multiply 4 × 2.
questions.stemEs: Una jardinera mide 4 pies de largo y 2 pies de ancho. ¿Cuál es su área?
questions.explanationEs: El área de un rectángulo es largo × ancho: 4 × 2 = 8 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: El área dice cuánto espacio plano cubre la jardinera.
Para un rectángulo, multiplica largo por ancho.
Multiplica 4 × 2.

questions.stem: That same planter is 4 feet long, 2 feet wide, and needs soil 1 foot deep. How much soil does the gardener need?
questions.explanation: Volume is length × width × depth: 4 × 2 × 1 = 8 cubic feet of soil.
choiceFeedback: 4 forgets to multiply by the width of 2.
7 comes from adding 4 + 2 + 1 instead of multiplying.
The number is right but soil fills space, so volume needs cubic units, not square units.
hints: Soil fills space, so you need volume.
Volume of a box is length × width × depth.
Multiply 4 × 2 × 1.
questions.stemEs: Esa misma jardinera mide 4 pies de largo, 2 pies de ancho y necesita tierra de 1 pie de profundidad. ¿Cuánta tierra necesita el jardinero?
questions.explanationEs: El volumen es largo × ancho × profundidad: 4 × 2 × 1 = 8 pies cúbicos de tierra.
hintsEs: La tierra llena espacio, así que necesitas el volumen.
El volumen de una caja es largo × ancho × profundidad.
Multiplica 4 × 2 × 1.

questions.stem: Leaving the water running while brushing wastes an average of 4 gallons per brushing. You brush twice a day. How much water can one person save per day by only turning the water on to rinse?
questions.explanation: 4 gallons saved per brushing × 2 brushings a day = 8 gallons a day.
choiceFeedback: 2 comes from dividing 4 by 2 instead of multiplying.
4 gallons is the savings for only ONE brushing — you brush twice a day.
6 comes from adding 4 + 2 instead of multiplying.
hints: How many gallons does one brushing save?
How many times do you brush each day?
Multiply 4 × 2.
questions.stemEs: Dejar el agua corriendo mientras te cepillas desperdicia en promedio 4 galones por cepillado. Te cepillas dos veces al día. ¿Cuánta agua puede ahorrar una persona al día si abre la llave solo para enjuagar?
questions.explanationEs: 4 galones ahorrados por cepillado × 2 cepillados al día = 8 galones al día.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántos galones ahorra un cepillado?
¿Cuántas veces te cepillas al día?
Multiplica 4 × 2.

level1.stem: A chef makes 10 sandwiches. Each sandwich uses 2 slices of cheese. How many slices of cheese does the chef need?
level1.stemEs: Un chef hace 10 sándwiches. Cada sándwich usa 2 rebanadas de queso. ¿Cuántas rebanadas de queso necesita el chef?
hints: Multiply the sandwiches by the slices in one sandwich.
hintsEs: Multiplica los sándwiches por las rebanadas de un sándwich.
level1.explanation: Write the known ratio in the table: 1 sandwich → 2 slices Find the scale factor from 1 sandwich to 10: 10 ÷ 1 = 10 Multiply the slices by 10 too: 2 × 10 = 20
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la razón conocida en la tabla: 1 sándwich → 2 rebanadas Halla el factor de escala de 1 sándwich a 10: 10 ÷ 1 = 10 Multiplica también las rebanadas por 10: 2 × 10 = 20

buildFigure.caption: Each sandwich uses 2 slices of cheese.
buildFigure.captionEs: Cada sándwich usa 2 rebanadas de queso.

level1.stem: A planter is 6 feet long, 2 feet wide and 1 foot deep. How many cubic feet of soil fill it?
level1.stemEs: Una jardinera mide 6 pies de largo, 2 pies de ancho y 1 pie de profundidad. ¿Cuántos pies cúbicos de tierra la llenan?
hints: Multiply length × width × depth.
hintsEs: Multiplica largo × ancho × profundidad.
level1.explanation: Multiply length × width: 6 × 2 = 12 Multiply by the depth: 12 × 1 = 12
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica largo × ancho: 6 × 2 = 12 Multiplica por la profundidad: 12 × 1 = 12

level1.stem: A planter is 4 feet long and 3 feet wide. What is its area?
level1.stemEs: Una jardinera mide 4 pies de largo y 3 pies de ancho. ¿Cuál es su área?
hints: Area covers flat space. Multiply the length by the width.
hintsEs: El área cubre un espacio plano. Multiplica el largo por el ancho.
level1.explanation: Multiply length × width: 4 × 3 = 12 Write the unit for area: 12 sq ft
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica largo × ancho: 4 × 3 = 12 Escribe la unidad del área: 12 sq ft

level1.stem: A cook puts 4 meatballs in each bowl of soup. She makes 12 bowls. How many meatballs does she need?
level1.stemEs: Una cocinera pone 4 albóndigas en cada plato de sopa. Hace 12 platos. ¿Cuántas albóndigas necesita?
hints: Each bowl has the same amount. Multiply the bowls by the meatballs in one bowl.
hintsEs: Cada plato tiene la misma cantidad. Multiplica los platos por las albóndigas de un plato.
level1.explanation: Write the known ratio in the table: 1 bowl → 4 meatballs Find the scale factor from 1 bowl to 12: 12 ÷ 1 = 12 Multiply the meatballs by 12 too: 4 × 12 = 48
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la razón conocida en la tabla: 1 plato → 4 albóndigas Halla el factor de escala de 1 plato a 12: 12 ÷ 1 = 12 Multiplica también las albóndigas por 12: 4 × 12 = 48

level1.stem: A planter is 8 feet long and 3 feet wide. What is its area?
level1.stemEs: Una jardinera mide 8 pies de largo y 3 pies de ancho. ¿Cuál es su área?
hints: Area covers flat space. Multiply the length by the width.
hintsEs: El área cubre un espacio plano. Multiplica el largo por el ancho.
level1.explanation: Multiply length × width: 8 × 3 = 24 Write the unit for area: 24 sq ft
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica largo × ancho: 8 × 3 = 24 Escribe la unidad del área: 24 sq ft

level2.stem: A planter is 5 feet long, 2 feet wide and 3 feet deep. Ana says she needs 10 cubic feet of soil. Which statement is correct?
level2.stemEs: Una jardinera mide 5 pies de largo, 2 pies de ancho y 3 pies de profundidad. Ana dice que necesita 10 pies cúbicos de tierra. ¿Qué afirmación es correcta?
hints: Ana used only two of the three measures. Which one did she leave out?
hintsEs: Ana usó solo dos de las tres medidas. ¿Cuál dejó fuera?
level2.explanation: See what Ana found: 5 × 2 = 10 Multiply by the depth too: 5 × 2 × 3 = 30
level2.explanationEs: Mira lo que halló Ana: 5 × 2 = 10 Multiplica también por la profundidad: 5 × 2 × 3 = 30
choices: Ana forgot the depth. She needs 30 cubic feet.
Ana is right. She needs 10 cubic feet.
choicesEs: Ana olvidó la profundidad. Necesita 30 pies cúbicos.
Ana tiene razón. Necesita 10 pies cúbicos.
choiceFeedback: 10 is the area, 5 × 2. Soil fills space, so multiply by the depth too.
Adding the sides does not find volume. Multiply length × width × depth.

level2.stem: A cafe expects 90 customers. 1 out of every 5 customers orders soup. Each bowl uses 3 cups of broth. How many cups of broth are needed?
level2.stemEs: Un café espera 90 clientes. 1 de cada 5 clientes pide sopa. Cada plato usa 3 tazas de caldo. ¿Cuántas tazas de caldo se necesitan?
hints: Find the part of the crowd first: how many customers order soup?
hintsEs: Primero halla la parte de la gente: ¿cuántos clientes piden sopa?
level2.explanation: Find the scale factor from 5 customers to 90: 90 ÷ 5 = 18 Multiply the soup orders by 18 too: 1 × 18 = 18 Multiply the bowls by the cups per bowl: 18 × 3 = 54
level2.explanationEs: Halla el factor de escala de 5 clientes a 90: 90 ÷ 5 = 18 Multiplica también los pedidos de sopa por 18: 1 × 18 = 18 Multiplica los platos por las tazas de cada uno: 18 × 3 = 54

buildFigure.caption: 1 out of every 5 customers orders soup.

level2.stem: A chef makes 18 tacos. Each taco uses 2 ounces of chicken. How many ounces of chicken does the chef need?
level2.stemEs: Un chef hace 18 tacos. Cada taco usa 2 onzas de pollo. ¿Cuántas onzas de pollo necesita el chef?
hints: Multiply the tacos by the ounces in one taco.
hintsEs: Multiplica los tacos por las onzas de un taco.
level2.explanation: Write the known ratio in the table: 1 taco → 2 oz Find the scale factor from 1 taco to 18: 18 ÷ 1 = 18 Multiply the ounces by 18 too: 2 × 18 = 36
level2.explanationEs: Escribe la razón conocida en la tabla: 1 taco → 2 oz Halla el factor de escala de 1 taco a 18: 18 ÷ 1 = 18 Multiplica también las onzas por 18: 2 × 18 = 36

buildFigure.caption: Each taco uses 2 ounces of chicken.
buildFigure.captionEs: Cada taco usa 2 onzas de pollo.

level2.stem: A planter is 8 feet long, 3 feet wide and 1.5 feet deep. How many cubic feet of soil fill it?
level2.stemEs: Una jardinera mide 8 pies de largo, 3 pies de ancho y 1.5 pies de profundidad. ¿Cuántos pies cúbicos de tierra la llenan?
hints: Find the area of the bottom first. Then multiply by the depth, 1.5.
hintsEs: Primero halla el área del fondo. Luego multiplica por la profundidad, 1.5.
level2.explanation: Find the area of the bottom: 8 × 3 = 24 Multiply by the depth: 24 × 1.5 = 36
level2.explanationEs: Halla el área del fondo: 8 × 3 = 24 Multiplica por la profundidad: 24 × 1.5 = 36

level2.stem: At home, a family puts a rug in the living room. The rug is 9 feet long and 6 feet wide. How many square feet of floor does it cover?
level2.stemEs: En casa, una familia pone un tapete en la sala. El tapete mide 9 pies de largo y 6 pies de ancho. ¿Cuántos pies cuadrados del piso cubre?
hints: The rug covers flat space. Find its area.
hintsEs: El tapete cubre un espacio plano. Halla su área.
level2.explanation: Multiply length × width: 9 × 6 = 54 Write the unit for area: 54 sq ft
level2.explanationEs: Multiplica largo × ancho: 9 × 6 = 54 Escribe la unidad del área: 54 sq ft

level3.stem: A gardener has 60 cubic feet of soil. Planter A is 5 by 4 by 2 feet. Planter B is 6 by 3 by 3 feet. Can she fill both planters?
level3.stemEs: Un jardinero tiene 60 pies cúbicos de tierra. La jardinera A mide 5 por 4 por 2 pies. La jardinera B mide 6 por 3 por 3 pies. ¿Puede llenar las dos jardineras?
hints: Find the volume of each planter. Then add them and compare with 60.
hintsEs: Halla el volumen de cada jardinera. Luego súmalos y compara con 60.
level3.explanation: Find the volume of each planter: 5 × 4 × 2 = 40; 6 × 3 × 3 = 54 Add the volumes: 40 + 54 = 94 Compare with the soil she has: 94 > 60
level3.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de cada jardinera: 5 × 4 × 2 = 40; 6 × 3 × 3 = 54 Suma los volúmenes: 40 + 54 = 94 Compara con la tierra que tiene: 94 > 60
choices: No. Together they need 94 cubic feet.
Yes. Each planter needs less than 60 cubic feet.
Yes. Their areas add to 38 square feet.
choicesEs: Sí. Cada jardinera necesita menos de 60 pies cúbicos.
Sí. Sus áreas suman 38 pies cuadrados.
choiceFeedback: Each one fits alone, but she must fill both. Add the volumes: 40 + 54 = 94.
Area does not tell how much soil fills a planter. Use volume, in cubic feet.

level3.stem: A diner expects 150 customers. 1 out of every 6 customers orders pancakes. Each order uses 3 eggs. How many eggs are needed?
level3.stemEs: Un restaurante espera 150 clientes. 1 de cada 6 clientes pide panqueques. Cada orden usa 3 huevos. ¿Cuántos huevos se necesitan?
hints: Find how many customers order pancakes first.
hintsEs: Primero halla cuántos clientes piden panqueques.
level3.explanation: Find the scale factor from 6 customers to 150: 150 ÷ 6 = 25 Multiply the pancake orders by 25 too: 1 × 25 = 25 Multiply the orders by the eggs in each: 25 × 3 = 75
level3.explanationEs: Halla el factor de escala de 6 clientes a 150: 150 ÷ 6 = 25 Multiplica también las órdenes de panqueques por 25: 1 × 25 = 25 Multiplica las órdenes por los huevos de cada una: 25 × 3 = 75

buildFigure.caption: 1 out of every 6 customers orders pancakes.

level3.stem: At home, a bedroom floor is 12 feet long and 10 feet wide. Carpet costs $4 for each square foot. How much does carpet for the whole floor cost?
level3.stemEs: En casa, el piso de una recámara mide 12 pies de largo y 10 pies de ancho. La alfombra cuesta $4 por cada pie cuadrado. ¿Cuánto cuesta alfombrar todo el piso?
hints: Carpet covers flat space. Find the area first, then multiply by the price.
hintsEs: La alfombra cubre un espacio plano. Primero halla el área y luego multiplica por el precio.
level3.explanation: Find the area of the floor: 12 × 10 = 120 Multiply by the price per square foot: 120 × 4 = 480
level3.explanationEs: Halla el área del piso: 12 × 10 = 120 Multiplica por el precio de cada pie cuadrado: 120 × 4 = 480

level3.stem: A garden bed is 7 feet long and 3 feet wide. The soil must be 1.5 feet deep. Soil comes in bags of 2 cubic feet. How many bags must the gardener buy?
level3.stemEs: Un cantero mide 7 pies de largo y 3 pies de ancho. La tierra debe tener 1.5 pies de profundidad. La tierra viene en bolsas de 2 pies cúbicos. ¿Cuántas bolsas debe comprar el jardinero?
hints: Find the volume. Divide by 2. The store sells only whole bags.
hintsEs: Halla el volumen. Divide entre 2. La tienda solo vende bolsas enteras.
level3.explanation: Find the volume of soil: 7 × 3 × 1.5 = 31.5 Divide by the cubic feet in one bag: 31.5 ÷ 2 = 15.75 Round up so the bed is full: 15.75 → 16
level3.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de tierra: 7 × 3 × 1.5 = 31.5 Divide entre los pies cúbicos de una bolsa: 31.5 ÷ 2 = 15.75 Redondea hacia arriba para que el cantero quede lleno: 15.75 → 16

level3.stem: Each person saves 2,920 gallons a year. Which correctly compares households of 3, 4, 5, and 8 people?
choiceFeedback: Those add the household size to 2,920 instead of multiplying by it.
20,440 is 7 × 2,920 — the last household has 8 people, not 7.
46,720 is 16 × 2,920 — that doubles the 8-person household instead of computing it.
hints: Each household total is people × 2,920.
Check the last value most carefully.
level3.stemEs: Cada persona ahorra 2,920 galones al año. ¿Cuál compara correctamente hogares de 3, 4, 5 y 8 personas?
hintsEs: El total de cada hogar es personas × 2,920.
Revisa el último valor con más cuidado.
